title: Naturality of the canonical Cech-to-cohomology comparison map
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal U:X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ be an open covering, viewed as a covering of the Zariski site of $X$ [def-sc-zariski-site]; write $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,-)$ and $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$ for its Cech complex and Cech cohomology [def-weil-pbc-site-cech-complex]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and $p\geq0$, the *canonical comparison map* $c_{\mathcal F}:\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is defined as follows. Choose an injective resolution $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-modules-enough-injectives], and let $T_{\mathcal F}$ be the total complex [def-sp-double-complex-total] of the first-quadrant double complex with terms $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)$. The restriction maps $\mathcal I^q(X)\to\check{\mathcal C}^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal I^q)$ give a cochain map $\alpha_{\mathcal F}:\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet)\to T_{\mathcal F}$ and $\mathcal F\to\mathcal I^0$ gives a cochain map $\beta_{\mathcal F}:\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to T_{\mathcal F}$. Then $\alpha_{\mathcal F}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $c_{\mathcal F}=H^p(\alpha_{\mathcal F})^{-1}\circ H^p(\beta_{\mathcal F})$, followed by the identification $H^p(\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^\bullet))=H^p(X,\mathcal F)$, does not depend on the choice of the resolution. These maps are natural in $\mathcal F$: for every morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and every $p\geq0$, $c_{\mathcal F'}\circ\check H^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)=H^p(X,\varphi)\circ c_{\mathcal F}$, where $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)$ is induced by the cochain map $(c_{i_0\dots i_p})\mapsto(\varphi(c_{i_0\dots i_p}))$.

proof.text: Use moduleCechAlpha_isIso from def-sc-module-cech-comparison in every degree and Mathlib quasiIso_iff to obtain the alpha quasi-isomorphism.

Install EnoughInjectives using moduleSheaves_abelian_enoughInjectives from lem-sc-ringed-space-module-sheaves-enough-injectives. Choose an injective resolution I and define c = H(beta_I) followed by the inverse of H(alpha_I) and the inverse resolution identification. These inverses exist by moduleCechAlpha_isIso. For a lift of a coefficient morphism, take homology of the alpha and beta squares of lem-sc-module-cech-lift-squares and use isoRightDerivedObj_hom_naturality; associativity gives comparison_transport. Applying it to the identity from I to an arbitrary resolution J proves that c satisfies IsModuleCechComparison for every J. For two given comparisons, apply comparison_transport and the equation for cG, then cancel the composite of the resolution identification and H(alpha_J). This proves naturality.
